talk_track: Ben Cole — I build the platform, security, and cost layer underneath founding teams so they stay on product; most recently that meant a first-attempt SOC 2 Type II at Lexipol in a CJIS-regulated environment, with AWS spend down 22% alongside. Kepler's live Platform Engineer posting is unusually candid: 'This is the first dedicated platform hire,' owning SOC 2 controls, in-VPC enterprise deployments, and the AWS account 'the whole company depends on.' Read plainly, that means the layer a bank's procurement team audits before your largest deals close is owned by nobody today. One IC rarely covers all of that, and the baseline is worth defining before the hire so they land on a paved road instead of an audit backlog. That gap is exactly the fractional work I do underneath founders while the permanent team takes shape. Which stalls deals sooner right now — SOC 2 evidence or the single-tenant deployment model?
